digest.component_or_area: op-cert service signing and key management
propositions: The op-cert service must accept exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY at startup, validate before service creation, and reject missing, duplicate, unreadable, non-regular, malformed, or non-Ed25519 inputs.

The validated key must be copied to a process-owned 0700 directory with 0600 file permissions, remain immutable for the process lifetime, observe replacements only after restart, and cleanup must never alter the deployment source.

Both out-of-opcert_service producer chains (completion via sign_completion_verdict and plan-review via generation.sign_manifest) must accept and use an optional context-local OpcertSigner binding instead of reading from os.environ, proving isolation across concurrent and timed-out jobs.

The op-cert application runtime must have no runtime SSM/boto3/region dependency; the key must be materialized before start by fetch-secrets.sh to a bind-mounted 0600 file with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH, and the compose service must not carry REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM or key-retrieval regions.
Developer-local signing paths (close/review-plan callers without a bound context) must retain environment/genesis-based resolution unchanged as a regression pin.
The shared /rebar/prod/* SSM grant in iam.tf co-used by origin-guard/gerrit must remain unchanged; only the op-cert app-runtime boundary is decoupled from SSM.
